definition: The art itself, officially *the Art of the Creator through the person of knowing and compassion*. ‘Jyutsu’ is a non-standard spelling of *jutsu*, art. A registered trademark in the US.
Person of knowing and compassion (benevolence).
Creator (spirit, divine).
Art; JSJ stresses it is an art, not a technique.
The body of JSJ theory taught alongside the hands-on work in the 5-Day Basic seminar.
Nature: stop, look within and listen. Understanding of oneself (SH2 pp.51, 65-66).
Nature: practical application. The method, the hands-on part (SH2 pp.51, 65-66).
Burmeister’s word for what tension in the flows becomes. She traces it to how we eat and live, to mental and emotional strain, to heredity and to injury.
One of 26 locations, paired on each side of the body: 23 on the Supervisor and 3 on the Mediator (SH2 p.8). Holding one helps unlock stagnation in the flows.
Notation for the upper or lower part of a lock that covers a larger area.
A layer of being and energy, from the most manifest (1st) to the least (9th). One instructor calls it a state of being that develops as we go.
One of five emotional habits, worry, fear, anger, grief and pretense (trying-to), that disharmonise the flows. Each is linked to a finger and a depth.
The attitude linked to the little finger and 5th Depth; also called trying too hard, or judgement.
Both an energy current along a set path in the body and the sequence of two-hand holds, on locks or body areas, that helps it along; context says which.
Metaphor for the two hands connecting two points so energy can move between them.
Holds and flows a person applies to themselves; taught from Burmeister's three Self-Help Books.
Short hold standing in for a full flow: for a lock in SH2, its finger or a pair of places.
The three Text 1 universal harmonizing energies: Main Central Vertical, Supervisor and Mediator.
The first and only single flow; descends the front and ascends the back; called the Source of Life.
Paired left and right universal harmonising energy that carries 23 of the 26 locks and supervises each side. Arises at Lock 1.
Paired energy that arises at Lock 3 and crosses the body, mediating between the sides and with the Main Central. The first flow attitudes affect.

japanese: 伊邪那岐 / 伊邪那美
definition: Names Murai reportedly gave the left and right Mediators, after the creator gods of Japanese myth (kanji from general Japanese usage, not from a JSJ source).
Text 1 term for the unmanifested, universal level of the flows (MCV, Supervisor, Mediator).
Text 2 term for the individualised energies of the 12 organ functions.
Flows of the 12 organ function energies, Lung through Liver, each active for about two hours in a 24-hour cycle.
The 6th Depth organ function (in Chinese medicine, Pericardium or Circulation-Sex). Father archetype; an ascending flow that governs the descending ones.
6th Depth organ function (TCM: Triple Warmer); mother archetype.
Text 2 holds for particular body functions, numbered SBF 1 to 5, plus related function holds.
Three short corrective sequences restoring the Mediator to itself, to the Supervisor, and to the Main Central.
Direction of energy: descending runs down the front with the exhale; ascending runs up the back with the inhale.

term: Bust line / Waist line / Hip line
definition: Three horizontal divisions of the body linked to lock pairs and to the Mediator, Main Central and Supervisor respectively.
Reading the depths at both wrists with three fingers each to choose flows, before and during a session.
In the Depths: a body part or sense organ through which a depth expresses itself (for example the ears for the 4th Depth). In SH1: a numbered set of self-help practices, I to IV.
Murai's eight hand poses, I to VIII in SH3 pp.9-16, used as self-help.
Burmeister’s two seminar texts. Text 1 covers the unmanifest universal level: the locks, the Trinity, the depths. Text 2 covers the organ function energies.
Advanced seminar of Jin Shin Jyutsu Inc.; from Burmeister's phrase about getting to know (help) myself.
Burmeister's framing of the art as getting to know (help) oneself.
Palms-together greeting used as a closing by some practitioners (kanji from general Japanese usage).

term: Ama no Minaka Nushi no Kami
definition: Japanese deity name quoted in an MCV article, glossed as the divine presence at the centre of the universe (kanji from general Japanese usage).
Status after three 5-Day seminars (105 hours) with Jin Shin Jyutsu Inc.

SH2 lists O, the oval, ahead of Number 1 (p.9) and writes of locks 0-26 (pp.26, 66-67), though she counts twenty-six (pp.6, 8). It is the Main Central itself, limitless light, the breath. Held with one hand on the crown and the other on the pubic bone or coccyx, or by holding the centre of each palm in turn (SH2 pp.9-11).
Burmeister's acronym: Fulfilling, Understanding, No-thing (SH2 p.65; SH3 p.1).
Burmeister's acronym: False Evidence Appearing Real (SH2 pp.20, 65).
